title: Patch: a replay names the opponent as its row in the replays list does
thread:
**Issue #3698 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #3698: Patch: a replay names the opponent as its row in the replays list does
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The replays list says "Win · vs Bob", but the replay it opens calls Bob only "Opponent", and a practice game's replay says "Opponent" though the live game said "AI · Easy". Once this is built, a replay labels the other side as the list and the live game did: the opponent's name for an online game, the AI and its level for practice.

## Why
- The online row names the opponent (`apps/web/src/routes/replays.tsx:451-455`; "a deleted account" when the name is gone).
- `ReplayPlayerProps` (`apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.tsx:33-43`) takes no label, so the opened board falls back to `Hero`'s default "Opponent" (`apps/web/src/game/Hero.tsx:210`), and the modifier list is handed "Opponent" (`ReplayPlayer.tsx:281`).
- The live practice board passes its label through `Game`'s `enemyLabel` (`apps/web/src/routes/practice.tsx:1081`, `:1116`); the replay of the same game drops it.
- The owner already wanted known seats named: a watched game and a friend's shared replay speak of the friend by name (#2019).

## Proposal
`ReplayPlayer` takes an optional `opponentLabel`, passed to `Game`'s `enemyLabel` and to `ModifierList`. Each caller fills it from what it already holds: the replays list from the row's opponent (the AI and its tier for a practice row), the practice result's replay from the live board's label, a match result's replay from the name the match screen already shows. A friend's shared-replay route keeps its own wording. A long name is cut with an ellipsis in `.hero-seat`. The shared GIF is unchanged, since it names no seat (R513000). Presentation only (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Where it lands
- `apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.tsx`, `apps/web/src/routes/replays.tsx`, `apps/web/src/routes/practice.tsx`, `apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx`, `apps/web/src/game/board.css`
- `apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.test.tsx`, `apps/web/src/routes/replays.test.tsx`, `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json` for any new string
- SPEC §9.5; R513000

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `ReplayPlayer` given `opponentLabel` "Bob#12" shows it on the opponent hero's seat label and in the modifier list; without it, "Opponent" as today.
- [ ] Opening an online row from the replays list labels the opponent with its username, "a deleted account" when it is empty; a practice row shows the AI's label.
- [ ] A practice game's replay shows the live board's label.
- [ ] A friend's shared replay and the shared GIF are unchanged.

## Size and risks
Small to medium: about five files and their tests. A replay opened from a link with no list row behind it has no name to show and keeps "Opponent".

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

Class: `polish` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it.

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-8` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43051727844)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

A replay labels the other side as the replays list and the live game do, not as a bare "Opponent".

- `ReplayPlayer` takes an optional `opponentLabel`. It goes to `Game`'s `enemyLabel` (the opponent hero's seat label) and to `ModifierList`'s `opponentLabel`. Without it, both stay "Opponent".
- The replays list fills it from the row. An online row gets the username, or "a deleted account" when the username is empty. A practice row gets the AI's label.
- A practice game's result replay uses the live board's label. A match result's replay uses the opponent's name from the match screen's ranks read.
- A long name is cut with an ellipsis in `.hero-seat`.
- A friend's shared replay (`TogetherRoute`), the shared GIF, JSON-opened replays and co-op replays are unchanged.

## Files to touch

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.tsx` | `change`: add optional `opponentLabel` to `ReplayPlayerProps`; use it in `Game` and `ModifierList` |
| `apps/web/src/routes/replays.tsx` | `change`: add `opponentLabel?` to the `Open` variant with a `source`; set it in `openPractice` and `openOnline`; pass it to `ReplayPlayer` |
| `apps/web/src/routes/practice.tsx` | `change`: hoist the `enemyLabel` const above the `watching` branch; pass `opponentLabel` to `ReplayPlayer` |
| `apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx` | `change`: derive the opponent's name from `ranks`; pass `opponentLabel` to `OpenedReplay` |
| `apps/web/src/game/board.css` | `change`: ellipsis on `.hero-seat` |
| `apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.test.tsx` | `change`: new tests |
| `apps/web/src/routes/replays.test.tsx` | `change`: extend or add tests |
| `apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx` | `change`: one new test |
| `apps/web/src/routes/practice.test.tsx` | `change`: one new test, if its replay-opening helper makes that cheap |

`OpenedReplay.tsx` needs no change, because its props are `Omit<ReplayPlayerProps, "source">` and it spreads them into `ReplayPlayer`. `zh-CN.json` needs no change, because every string used (`AI`, `Opponent`, `a deleted account`, `Easy`, `Sandbox`) already has an entry. The spec cites R513000, but its ruling note and §9.5 need no edit. This is presentation only (CLAUDE.md rule 7), so there is no new ruling and no `spec/pending` file.

Do not touch: `crates/`, `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `ShareGif.tsx`, `TogetherRoute.tsx`, `DuosReplay.tsx`, `Hero.tsx`, `Game.tsx`, `Board.tsx`, `ModifierList.tsx`, or `apps/web/src/wire/`.

## Steps

1. **`ReplayPlayer.tsx`**
   - In `ReplayPlayerProps` add `/** The other side's name on the board and in the modifier list, already translated: the list's opponent, the AI and its level. Absent, "Opponent". */ opponentLabel?: string;`.
   - Destructure it in `ReplayPlayer({...})`.
   - On `<Game>` add `enemyLabel={opponentLabel}`. `Game`'s `enemyLabel?: string` accepts `undefined`, as `practice.tsx` already passes it, so a plain pass-through works.
   - Change `<ModifierList view={at.step.view} opponentLabel={opponentLabel ?? t("Opponent")} />`.

2. **`replays.tsx`**
   - Extend the first `Open` variant to `{ key: string; source: ReplaySource; matchId?: string; practice?: true; opponentLabel?: string }`.
   - In `openPractice`, add `opponentLabel: t("AI")` to the `setOpen` object. The listing (`PracticeReplayListing`) carries no difficulty, and adding one means a `crates/shared` wire change, which is out of scope; see Open questions.
   - In `openOnline`, add `opponentLabel: row.opponent.username === "" ? t("a deleted account") : row.opponent.username`. Pull the expression into a small module-level helper, `function opponentName(row: OnlineReplayListing): string`, and use it in the row render as well (`const opponent = opponentName(row);`). The list and the replay then cannot drift apart.
   - In the `ReplayPlayer` element in the `open !== null` branch, spread `{...(open.opponentLabel === undefined ? {} : { opponentLabel: open.opponentLabel })}`, next to the existing `actions` spread. A file-opened replay (`OpenReplayJson`) sets no label and keeps "Opponent".

3. **`practice.tsx`**
   - Cut the `const enemyLabel = ...` block, with its comment, from below the `watching` branch (about line 1089).
   - Paste it just before `if (watching !== null && watching.game === game && replaySource !== null)`, about line 1035. `config` is already known non-null there, from the guard above.
   - Add `{...(config.lesson === undefined ? { opponentLabel: enemyLabel } : {})}` to the `<ReplayPlayer>` there. A lesson draws no label live, so it draws none in its replay.
   - Leave the later `enemyLabel={config.lesson === undefined ? enemyLabel : undefined}` as it is.

4. **`match.tsx`**
   - Near `const moves`, after `ranks` is available, add `const opponentSeat = ranks === null ? undefined : (["p1", "p2"] as const).map((side) => ranks.seats[side]).find((seat) => !seat.you);` and `const opponentName = opponentSeat?.username === "" ? undefined : opponentSeat?.username;`.
   - Do this before the `watching !== null && view.result !== null` early return (about line 402), since that return comes first. `ranks` comes from the `useMatchRanks` hook at line 203, so it is in scope. The spot is after the hooks and before that return, so the new lines add no hook.
   - On `<OpenedReplay>` there, add `{...(opponentName === undefined ? {} : { opponentLabel: opponentName })}`.
   - If the ranks read has not arrived or has no names, the label stays "Opponent".
   - Do not touch the live `<Game>` or its `ModifierList` in `match.tsx`; the issue asks only for the replay.

5. **`board.css`**
   - In `.hero-seat` (line 177) add `min-width: 0; max-width: 14ch; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap;`. `.hero` is a no-wrap flex row.
   - Add a one-line comment saying a long name is cut with an ellipsis, as `username.css` does.
   - Cutting it can only shorten a label, so "AI · Easy" at 14ch uppercase must still fit. If the builder is unsure, widen to 18ch.

6. **Tests**, in the files listed below.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.test.tsx`, reusing the `open()` helper and `withModifiersAt()`. Extend `open()` with an optional third parameter `opponentLabel?: string`, passed as a prop, or render `ReplayPlayer` directly.
  - `it("#3698 opponentLabel names the opponent hero's seat and the modifier list", ...)`:
    - Open with `opponentLabel="Bob#12"`, using `fakeReplaySource(withModifiersAt(k))` with `k = laterStep()`, then jump to `k`.
    - Assert the opponent hero's `.hero-seat` text is "Bob#12". Use `document.querySelector(".hero-opponent .hero-seat")`, after checking in `Hero.tsx` and `Board.tsx` that the hero root carries `hero-opponent`; otherwise find it via `testid` in `game/contract.ts`.
    - Assert the viewer's seat still reads "You".
    - Click `modifierListTestid.chip` and assert `modifierListTestid.panel` contains "Bob#12".
  - `it("#3698 without opponentLabel the seat and the modifier list say Opponent", ...)`: the same without the prop, expecting "Opponent" in both. CSS uppercase does not change `textContent`.
- `apps/web/src/routes/replays.test.tsx`:
  - In the existing "R768000 signed in, lists the account's online games…" test, or a new `it("#3698 an online row's replay names its opponent, a deleted account when the name is gone", ...)`, open row `m-1` (username "rival") and assert the opened board's `.hero-opponent .hero-seat` reads "rival". Open `m-2` (empty username) and assert it reads "a deleted account". Follow the existing `serveSteps()`, `renderRoute` and Back patterns.
  - Add `it("#3698 a practice row's replay labels the opponent AI", ...)` after the first test's `storeWithGame()`: click Watch and assert the seat reads "AI".
- `apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx`: one `it("#3698 …")`. Open the match replay after a result, with the ranks body `ranksBody` (p1 `you: true`, p2 `you: false`), and assert the replay's opponent seat shows p2's username. If driving a finished match to the replay is more than a small addition, instead assert via a mocked `OpenedReplay` or `ReplayPlayer` that the prop is passed. If neither is cheap, say so in the final report rather than skip silently.
- `apps/web/src/routes/practice.test.tsx`: only if a test already opens a practice result replay, add an assertion that its seat reads the live label ("AI · Easy" for the default difficulty; read the `DIFFICULTY_LABEL` text from `practice/Tier.tsx`).
- A friend's shared replay and the GIF are unchanged because their code is untouched. The existing `TogetherRoute`, `opening.test.tsx` and ShareGif tests cover them. Run `opening.test.tsx` too.

Commands, from the repository root:

- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/replay/ReplayPlayer.test.tsx`
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/replay/opening.test.tsx`
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/replays.test.tsx`
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/match.test.tsx`
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/practice.test.tsx`
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/replay apps/web/src/routes apps/web/src/game/board.css`, where the eslint pattern should name `.tsx` files only.

## Done when

- [ ] `ReplayPlayer` with `opponentLabel="Bob#12"` shows it on the opponent seat and in the modifier list; without it, "Opponent".
- [ ] An online row from the replays list opens labelled with its username, "a deleted account" when empty. A practice row opens labelled "AI".
- [ ] A practice game's replay shows the live board's label, none for a lesson.
- [ ] A match result's replay shows the opponent's username when the ranks read has it.
- [ ] A long name is ellipsised in `.hero-seat`.
- [ ] A friend's shared replay, the shared GIF, file-opened replays and co-op replays are unchanged.
- [ ] The new tests and the web test files touched pass.
- [ ] Typecheck and eslint are clean.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo jackioh spec check` are untouched by this change and still pass.
- [ ] No new `eslint-disable`, `@ts-ignore`, `.skip` or `.only`.

## Risks

- **`match.tsx` hook order.** The `opponentName` lines go after all the hooks and plain consts, before the `watching` return. They add no hook, so they do not change hook order.
- **`practice.tsx` hoist.** `enemyLabel` is hoisted above a branch that returns early, which is safe because it is a plain expression. Check that `DIFFICULTY_LABEL`, `config.sandbox` and `config.difficulty` are the same names as the original block.
- **Labels sent to the board.** `Game`'s `enemyLabel` is a plain override, so it reaches no engine or hidden information; usernames come only from the list and ranks reads the client already holds (R1436 usernames, never profile ids). Do not put `profileId` in a label.
- **Hero width.** The `.hero` width is fixed (`--hero-w`), so a long name must not push the layout. That is the purpose of the ellipsis.

## Open questions

- A practice row in the replays list shows "AI", not "AI · Easy", because `PracticeReplayListing` / `PracticeReplaySummary` (`crates/shared/src/host/practice/types.rs`) hold no difficulty. The list row itself says only "Practice". Showing the tier would add a field to a kept replay and its generated `wire/` types, which the reviewer should size as a cross-crate change. The plan does not do it. A person can approve it as a follow-up.
- On the match screen, the live board still says "Opponent". Only its replay gains the name, per the issue.
```
